newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firmer, with light products leading.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firmer, with light products leading.

text.p: European crude oil and refined product swaps were broadly firmer on Wednesday, despite the lacklustre performance of most futures markets, traders said.

Weekly stocks data showing a sharp fall in U.S. gasoline stocks pulled gasoline higher in the U.S. and this prised open the arbitrage window from Europe, leaving gasoline cargo markets tight in the region.
Naphtha was very strong, too. Fresh demand was expected from Asia and trader support to prompt prices in Europe contributed to August swaps' rise to around $188 cif NWE.

Brent contracts for differences (cfds) were a little firmer, too, amid signs of a tightening situation in the prompt physical markets. A cfd for the week August 4-8 traded at September -20, compared with -22 earlier.
A prompt Brent traded on Wednesday at August -3 cents, a gain of nine cents a barrel from the previous trade.
Fuel oil was only slightly firmer but barge markets were relatively thinly talked.
July swaps changed hands at $87.50 a tonne and August was talked around 50 cents higher than that. Physical markets hovered around $88/$88.50 a tonne for most of the day.
